why are borewells drying up in so many places

Groundwater behaves like a bank account, not a tap. Rain seeps down through soil and rock slowly, but a motor pump lifts in a day what took years to store, so run thousands at once and the water table drops, shallow wells failing first. Chennai's reservoirs ran nearly empty in 2019, which is why rooftop rainwater harvesting is taken seriously here. 💧 [STEPS]rain lands on your roof|pipes take it to a filter pit|water soaks down and refills the well[/STEPS] [CHIPS]Explain the water table|Does harvesting really work[/CHIPS]

what is the exact number of people alive on earth right now

Roughly eight billion — and the rounding is the honest part, not a cop-out. 🌍 An exact figure can't exist: someone is born and someone dies every few seconds, and no census counts everyone at the same instant. Those live counters online are models running a formula, not headcounts. [FACT]Roughly eight billion people are alive on Earth today.[/FACT] A rounded number that's true beats a precise one that's invented. [CHIPS]How censuses work|Why round numbers?|Population growth[/CHIPS]
is it true kids learn languages faster than teenagers

Partly true, and the honest version is more interesting. 🧠 Young children usually end up with a more native-sounding accent, because the ear tunes early to the sounds around it. But teenagers pick up grammar and vocabulary faster — you can hold a rule in your head that a five-year-old simply cannot. So you are not too late; you are strong at different parts of the job.
[CHIPS]Best age to start|How accents work|Tips for teenagers[/CHIPS]

how would i estimate how many people are at a temple festival

Estimating is not guessing — it is counting something small and scaling up 🔢. Count the people across one row, count how many rows deep the crowd runs, then multiply: twenty across and thirty deep is roughly six hundred. Then sanity-check it — could that space even hold six hundred people? Good estimates arrive as a range, never as one confident number. [CHIPS]Estimate my classroom|Why ranges matter|Try a bus queue[/CHIPS]

how does compound interest actually work

Simple interest pays you only on your original amount. Compound interest pays you on the interest too, so the pile starts feeding itself 📈. Take 100 rupees growing at 10% a year: year one adds 10 to make 110; year two earns 10% of 110, landing on 121 — not 120. That extra rupee is the whole trick, and it snowballs. Work out year three. [CHIPS]Check year three|Simple versus compound|Doubling time[/CHIPS]

why is voting kept secret

Because a vote someone can watch you cast isn't really yours. 🗳️ If a landlord, employer or neighbour could see the mark, they could reward it or punish it — so you vote behind a screen, and not even the polling officer learns your choice. Secrecy protects the weakest voter far more than the strongest one. That is why the booth has a screen, why phones are not allowed inside, and why nobody can make you say what you pressed. why does adding up the digits tell you if a number divides by 9

Because every place value is one more than a run of nines. Take 342, which is 3 hundreds + 4 tens + 2, and notice 100 is 99 + 1 while 10 is 9 + 1. Peel off the 99s and the 9s — already divisible by 9 — and all that remains is 3 + 4 + 2 = 9 🎯. The digit sum carries the whole remainder, which is why the trick works for 3 as well. why do websites not store your actual password

Because a stolen database should not hand over your login. Sites store a hash instead: a one-way scramble that is easy to run forwards and impractical to run backwards. When you sign in they hash what you typed and compare scrambles, never the password itself — which is why a real site can reset your password but can never tell you the old one. 🔐 Good sites pick a deliberately slow hash too, so guessing millions of passwords stays expensive. is recycling actually worth it or just for show

Every dinosaur roar you have ever heard was built by a sound engineer out of living animals. 🦕 Voice boxes are soft tissue and almost never fossilise, so nobody has the real sound and nobody ever will.
